precedence_order: 2. Board-issued policy in governance/ (security, compliance, hiring, conduct).
rule: When documents disagree, lower-precedence may add constraints but never relax them set higher up. Lower level NUMBER = HIGHER precedence = wins a direct conflict.

scenarios.description: engineering/CLAUDE.md (the Engineering dept charter) says a PR needs one reviewer approval before merge. engineering/agents/qa-eng/AGENTS.md (the QA Engineer role overlay) says a QA Engineer's own PRs may self-merge without review. The two conflict — which one governs?

governance/charter.md states the company charter requires board sign-off on any budget over $10k. A board-issued security policy document living under governance/ states security-tooling purchases under $50k are pre-approved without board sign-off. The two conflict — which one governs?

product/AGENTS.md (the Product dept's runtime instructions) tells every product role to skip the discovery-gate for goals under $1k. The root AGENTS.md org spec requires the Founder discovery gate for every new goal regardless of size. The two conflict — which one governs?

design/agents/product-designer/AGENTS.md (the Product Designer role overlay) says the Product Designer may work two tickets at once when both are trivial. design/AGENTS.md (the Design dept's runtime instructions) enforces WIP = 1 for every role without exception. The two conflict — which one governs?
